thread:
cs-rep: FYI customer ACME (ticket #C-1921) reports a realtime API p99 jump from ~220ms -> ~1.8s in eu-west starting ~2025-11-03 02:14 UTC. They see timeouts and a big tail on small-batch requests. This coincides with last night's infra rollout (driver + CUDA update). link: https://acme.support/tickets/C-1921

oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-20251103-9876543210 - p99 realtime latency spike (eu-west). Paging infra oncall.

infra-engr: Thanks. Can you paste the # requests/time window and a sample stack trace/log? Also which model variant and instance types are hitting the most?

cs-rep: Summary from customer: ~12% requests hit >1s p99, errors ~0.4%. Model: realtime-small-batch v2 @ gpu-a100-40 (shared pool). Spike began right after 02:10 UTC (we rolled driver 525.85 -> 526.x at 02:00 across eu-west). I attached traces and a flamegraph to the ticket.

support-lead: Marking as priority-high. If this is driver-related we should roll back canary and isolate traffic. cc @infra-engr @alex

alex: On it. First quick probe: can we get iostat + nvme stats + nvidia-smi on an affected host? Commands I usually ask for:``` 
iostat -x 1 10
sudo nvme top -t 1 -d /dev/nvme0n1
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,name,utilization.gpu,utilization.memory,temperature.gpu,compute_mode --format=csv
sudo dmesg | tail -n 200
``` 

jamie: Also collect /proc/interrupts and the kernel scheduling debug counters, and the instance's block device queue settings:``` 
cat /proc/interrupts | egrep "nvme|nvme0"
for d in /sys/block/nvme*; do echo $d; cat $d/queue/nr_requests; cat $d/queue/scheduler; done
``` 

cs-rep: Pasted key bits from one affected host (timestamps match 02:12 - 02:18):
```
> iostat -x 1 5
Device            r/s     w/s   rkB/s   wkB/s  avgrq-sz  avgqu-sz  await  svctm  %util
nvme0n1         120.5    3.2  9834.0   64.0    85.2     2.41    12.8   0.20  98.5
nvme1n1          10.1    0.9   120.0    8.0     20.4     0.02     1.5   0.12   1.2
```

cs-rep: And dmesg has repeated lines like:```
[Nov03 02:11:42] nvme nvme0: I/O submission delayed by host scheduler (competing load)
[Nov03 02:11:42] nvidia-modeset: GPU 0 microcode warning: submission latency high
```

infra-engr: Interesting — nvme0 is pegged. Looks like a single NVMe device is getting saturated (high avg queue, %util ~98). That would explain long tail for small-batch realtime requests which are IO-sensitive due to KV-pagecache flushes. Did the driver change alter submission batching or preemption paths?

fw-team: We saw a microcode change in the new driver that changed submission ordering on some SKUs. We're looking at a repro matrix but need a live sample.

alex: Short mitigation plan proposal: 1) Route impacted customer's realtime traffic to a fallback pool (cpu-backed or dedicated nvme stripe) 2) Reduce burst window via token bucket (rate-limit per-customer) 3) Roll back driver on canary nodes and hold rollout 4) Enable per-node host IO throttle (cgroups blkio or bfq/mq-deadline tweak) 5) Collect perf counters for nvme/blk/mq to confirm cause. Anyone object?

support-lead: Do it. Prioritize customer-facing mitigation (1+2) first. Notify CS.

jamie: Implemented rate-limit on customer's route to 60 rps and switched them to the dedicated-small pool (lower latency observed so far). Command used on edge-router:``` 
# route update
redwoodctl routes update --customer acme --route realtime --max-rps 60 --pool dedicated-small-eu
``` 

cs-rep: ACME reports p99 down to ~420ms after switch, errors dropped to 0.05%. They want ETA for permanent fix.

infra-engr: Rolling back driver on canary set now (5 nodes). Patch: revert to 525.85 binary and restart inference service. I'll post rollout logs.

alex: While rollback runs, collect perf snapshots every 30s:``` 
pidstat -d 1 10
perf record -a -o /tmp/perf-before.data -g sleep 10
sudo blktrace -d /dev/nvme0n1 -o - | blkparse -i - | head -n 200
``` 

infra-engr: Rollback completed on canary at 02:46 UTC. Early signals: nvme0 avgqu-sz down from 2.4 -> 0.05, %util -> 12%. p99 for ACME trending to ~230ms. Rolling out hold for rest of eu-west.

fw-team: We got a crashlog from driver 526.x showing a change in submission ordering flags that can cause head-of-line NVMe queue serialization on some firmware versions. We'll open FW-692 ticket to coordinate microcode patch + driver tweak.

support-lead: Great. Next steps: 1) Keep ACME on dedicated-small for 24h while we monitor 2) Block further 526.x rollout until fw-team confirms safe combo 3) Create postmortem and customer-facing summary.

cs-rep: Noted. I've updated the support ticket with a summary and the mitigation steps + ETA for next update. ACME wants a status update tomorrow morning their time.

alex: Added follow-up items: a) expand smoke checks to include nvme queue depth metrics b) add automatic routing fallback for high host-io cases c) add driver/firmware compatibility gate to rollout pipeline.

jamie: Also adding a temporary kernel knob to reduce request batching on hot nodes (mq-deadline options) as a stopgap for similar incidents. Will document exact sysctl we used in the runbook.

infra-engr: Closing live triage. Creating incident task list and assigning owners (FW: fw-team -> FW-692, Infra: alex -> ROLLBACK-958, Observability: jamie -> OBS-402).

oncall-bot: INC-20251103-9876543210 status: resolved (mitigated) -> followups created.

cs-rep: Customer notified, they appreciate quick rollback and the dedicated lane. Leaving ticket open until FW fix. Thanks all :slightly_smiling_face:
